source: CGZ arXiv:1712.04887v3 Theorem 1.2, Remark 1.9, Proposition 2.5; Addenda 32-35 (this repo)

result.m2_verdict: CGZ Theorem 1.2 never applies at n = 2 in any field of characteristic != 2: -1 is a nontrivial square root of 1, so F_2 = F, G is trivial, w_F is even, and only R^{w_F} is defined -- which is 1 in a group of exponent 2. There is no non-vacuous m = 2 invariant to compute, so the +1 of PR #4968 is forced by the group rather than measured.

scope: scope-(a) CENSUS of where a value can exist, not a value at any new m. Over F = Q_5 (the degree-1 place of K = Q(alpha)), for each m | 24 the class group F_m^x/(F_m^x)^m is Z/m x Z/m and the chi^{-1}-eigenspace is computed by brute force over all m^2 classes with the actual Frobenius action, then checked against the closed form m . gcd(m, 4). Three-way split: m | 4 has trivial Gal, a vacuous eigenspace and no value; m = 3 satisfies gcd(m, w_F) = 1 with w_{Q_5} = 4 so the lift is unique (the case already computed); m in {6, 8, 12, 24} has a proper eigenspace but gcd > 1, so only R^{w_F} is defined -- and that power is still non-trivial there, so information survives. Corrects the guess that queued this work: mu_m lies in Q_5 exactly when m | 4, NOT when m shares a factor with 4, so 8, 12 and 24 qualify. Also corrects a claim repeated throughout this arc: m = 2 is vacuous in EVERY field of characteristic != 2, because -1 forces F_2 = F and w_F even, so Theorem 1.2 never applies at n = 2 and only R^{w_F} = 1 is defined. The +1 of PR #4968 is forced by the group, not measured -- which does not make that computation wrong, but makes it empty as a CGZ value. Nothing wired.
